items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: for the Lester Youngs of the world, at that time, because jazz wasn’t codified into books

ctx.x: I think Dizzy, James Moody, Sonny Stitt, Wes Montgomery. I mean these are people that just were characters. But they had a lot of excellence. You don’t have to just be a fool. You know nobody wants to be around that. And so in a sense we are not allowing the characters to come through all this, because there’s a lot of cookie cutters now. There’s a lot of — and it’s really hard for the character to come through now, because there’s probably a little more suppressed stuff for someone who wants to go this way and…

Was it, I don’t know if “easier” is the right word, but for the Lester Youngs of the world, at that time, because jazz wasn’t codified into books and so forth, was it easier for him to be an individual? Nowadays there’s all the books to buy.

I think so. And yet I don’t know. He was different enough — I mean Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker, they were different enough, but even the black community didn’t want to hear the stuff that they were coming up with because it was different than what they were doing or what they were used to, or it wasn’t part of the church, whatever. So I think anybody who really wants to go over here is looked kind of down on. And yet, that same mass of people who are not, if they stay individual long enough, then they…
